title: Adaptive continuous-batching scheduler: fairness, starvation guard, and dynamic timeouts
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: Continuous batching improved throughput but exposed latency tail sensitivity under heterogeneous request mixes and long-lived KV cache hits. This PR introduces an adaptive scheduler layer that balances throughput and latency by applying fair queueing across priority lanes, a starvation detector that forces aging of stalled requests, and dynamic timeout windows for batch formation. Approach: 1) Add a lightweight multi-lane queue where requests are assigned a lane based on model variant, request size, and SLO tag; lane weights are tunable. 2) Implement priority aging: requests increment an urgency score while waiting; once score crosses a threshold they are promoted to a higher-service lane to prevent starvation. 3) Introduce adaptive batch-timeout calculation using recent interarrival statistics and per-lane latency SLOs; timeouts shorten for latency-sensitive lanes and lengthen for high-throughput lanes. 4) Starvation guard: per-queue watchdog that triggers a flush when the oldest request exceeds a configurable max-wait. 5) KV-cache-aware batching: prefer grouping requests with contiguous KV cache prefixes to reduce cache misses; integrates with existing cache index metadata. 6) Metrics and tracing hooks: new counters/gauges for lane sizes, promoted-count, starvation-flushes, timeout-adj-steps and histogram of batch formation delays. Backwards compatibility: Scheduler parameters default to previous single-queue behavior when feature flags disabled. Tests: unit tests for lane assignment, aging/promotion, timeout adaptation logic; integration tests exercising mixed-load scenarios and KV cache affinity. Benchmarks: On a mixed workload (70% short chat queries, 30% long-context summarization) we observe p50 latency unchanged, p95 reduced from 890ms to 560ms (35% improvement) for latency-sensitive lane and overall tokens/sec within 3% of prior baseline. Rollout: staged feature-flag rollout with Canary=10% -> 30% -> 100% with canary metrics smoke checks (p50/p95, error-rate, throughput) and auto-rollback on SLO regressions. Follow-ups: expose lane-weight tuning in console and provide a suggested tuning guide under redwood-docs.

review_comments: Marco Li: Strong direction. Two concerns: how do we ensure cache-affinity grouping doesn't starve small latency-sensitive requests when a large batch could be formed? Please add explicit tests that simulate a persistent stream of cache-coherent large requests alongside sparse latency-sensitive ones.

Priya Desai (author): Good point — added the starvation guard and priority aging to address exactly that scenario and added an integration test 'scheduler_mixed_load_test.py' that models the behavior. See commits d4b2e99 and 9d6c1aa.

Eleanor Shaw: Need to be careful with the interarrival estimator — smoothing window must not be too large for bursty traffic. Suggest exposing smoothing factor as a tuning knob and defaulting to a shorter window for latency lanes.
Priya Desai (author): Exposed smoothing_factor in config and added docs recommending 50-200ms effective window for chat workloads.
Jun Park: CI observed a flaky test in the first run (integration/scheduler_mixed_load_test) — was it root-caused?
Priya Desai (author): Flake was due to test harness timeouts; increased orchestration timeout and added deterministic seed to workload generator. Reran CI and all tests passed.
Marco Li: Approved after CI fixes and benchmark numbers look good.
Eleanor Shaw: Small comment: consider adding an alert if promoted-count spikes unexpectedly; can be follow-up.
Priya Desai (author): Agreed — queued as ENG-4278 follow-up to wire alerts and console tuning UI.
Release Manager (automated): Verified migration safe and feature flag default off for tenants with strict SLOs.
ci_checks: perf-regression: pass (p95 improved in canary run)
release_notes: Adaptive continuous-batching scheduler with fairness lanes, starvation prevention, and KV-cache-aware batching. Improves latency tail for mixed workloads while preserving throughput. Feature gated behind 'adaptive_scheduler' flag. See docs/scheduler_tuning.md for tuning guidance.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: adaptive_scheduler. Default false. Recommended canary cadence: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with 2h observation window. Key metrics: scheduler.lane_size.*, scheduler.starvation_flushes, scheduler.promotion_rate, batch.formation_delay.histogram. If p95 increases by >15% on canary, rollback the flag and notify infra-sre.
